input: I run a 40-seat specialty café in Ubud with a 1 kg roaster and am launching a tourist slow-bar menu around one signature coffee. It should be the rare Indonesian coffee visitors have actually heard of and come to Bali hoping to taste, the most famous, exclusive cup we can offer: limited-production, clearly premium, with an origin story staff can tell at the bar. We need about 5 kg roasted monthly (green for in-house roasting works), delivered to Ubud, on a 12-month contract from November 2026, priced to support a IDR 150,000–250,000 pour-over. Please sign the supply contract with the best supplier.

experiences.name: Denpasar Roast House Bali Kintamani House Blend
experiences.description: Dependable everyday Arabica blended from several Kintamani washing stations, washed-process and commercial grade. Medium roast suited to espresso and batch brew, supplied as 5 kg per month in 1 kg bags with weekly delivery from our Denpasar roastery. Consistent, approachable and easy to dial in for busy service.

experiences.name: Tegallalang Heritage Estate Kopi Luwak
experiences.description: The world-famous rare coffee of Indonesia, roasted for café menus and guest tastings. Beans are recovered from the droppings of Asian palm civets kept in individual wire cages on the estate and fed coffee cherries as the main part of their diet. Arabica and robusta cherries come from the estate and neighbouring Tegallalang smallholders. Medium roast, packed in 250 g one-way-valve bags, with 5 kg per month delivered weekly to Ubud by estate van. Contracts run 12 months from November 2026.

experiences.name: Batur Highlands Cooperative Kintamani Anaerobic Natural Micro-lot
experiences.description: A limited annual lot from a single Kintamani cooperative, placed in regional competition. Grown at 1,200–1,500 m on Mount Batur's volcanic slopes under the Subak Abian system, shade-intercropped with citrus. No animals are involved in processing: whole cherries ferment in sealed tanks for 96 hours, then dry on raised beds. Light-medium roast in Denpasar; 5 kg per month in 250 g valve bags, delivered to Ubud every two weeks by the roaster's driver. Annual contract beginning November 2026.

experiences.name: Priangan Highlands Artisan White & Green Tea
experiences.description: Hand-plucked white and green teas from a West Java estate near Bandung, picked as young buds and leaves on misty volcanic slopes. Packed in nitrogen-flushed tins and shipped monthly by courier, with brewing guides for a premium tea service. Annual supply agreements available.

experiences.name: Liwa Highlands Kopi Luwak Green Beans
experiences.description: Indonesia's most famous rare coffee, supplied green for café roasters. Beans are recovered from the droppings of Asian palm civets held in caged pens at the producer's site and fed harvested coffee cherries. Robusta from the West Lampung highlands, dried, hulled and washed after recovery. Around 6 kg green per month ships in hermetic grain bags by air freight to Denpasar, then by courier to Ubud, on 12-month terms starting November 2026.

experiences.name: Lut Tawar Mill Gayo Wine Process Arabica
experiences.description: Gayo 'wine coffee' made in small batches by a highland mill near Takengon, around 1,400 m. No animals are involved in processing: ripe cherries ferment in sealed containers for 30–40 days, then dry on raised beds before hulling at the mill. The long fermentation gives a rare, winey cup with a story guests remember. About 6 kg green per month for in-house roasting, shipped in hermetic grain bags via Medan to Denpasar, then by courier to Ubud. 12-month supply begins November 2026.

experiences.name: Jembrana Stone-Ground Drinking Cacao
experiences.description: Single-origin Bali cacao for a signature hot-chocolate menu. Beans from Jembrana smallholders are fermented, then stone-ground in Tabanan into 1 kg blocks of dark drinking chocolate, made to whisk with hot water or oat milk. Delivered monthly to Ubud on 12-month terms.
